back: The variety of life in an area: species diversity, genetic diversity and habitat diversity.
The number of different species in an area and how evenly individuals are spread among them.
Variety of genes within one species, e.g. local varieties of sorghum or indigenous chickens.
The variety of habitats in an area, e.g. woodland, grassland, vlei, kopje and river bank.
Goods are products (timber, fuel, food, medicines). Services are processes (soil protection, water regulation, pollination, carbon storage).

front: Small businesses that can use woodland sustainably
back: Beekeeping, eco-tourism, crafts from grass and reeds, processing wild fruits, tree nurseries.

front: What makes a resource-based business sustainable?
back: The resource is harvested no faster than it can recover, so it lasts for future use.

front: Why is a monoculture low in biodiversity?
back: One crop is planted and other plants are removed by weeding, ploughing or chemicals.
